subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the embedded macOS Dashboard browser receive only configured shared gateway token/password auth, or may it also reuse native device/operator tokens?
rationale: The linked bug frames native-token browser injection as a credential-boundary problem, while the sibling open PR depends on native/operator-token parity; automation cannot pick that product/security boundary safely.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
options.body: Require this PR or a replacement to exclude native device tokens from all macOS Dashboard browser injections, including endpoint reloads.

options.title: Use native-token parity
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue with the sibling parity direction if native device/operator tokens are intended to authenticate the embedded browser.

options.title: Add explicit compatibility mode
options.body: Keep shared-token/password behavior as the default and allow native-token browser injection only behind an intentional documented opt-in with tests.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser auth
recommendation.body: Require this PR or a replacement to exclude native device tokens from all macOS Dashboard browser injections, including endpoint reloads.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced and recently updated the native Dashboard surface, including the endpoint reload path now affected by this branch.
